title: Wildfire Smoke Affects Mothers' Employment
discussion_signal: The NBER relay links intermittent wildfire-smoke disruptions to school-based care with reduced mothers' employment even when formal care exists. A comment adds a possible labor-pool response—temporary workers or substitute staffing—without claiming that it resolves the care disruption.
linked_research_question: How do intermittent environmental disruptions to school-based care become labor-market shocks for mothers, and what forms of backup capacity can absorb them?
limits: Post is a concise research relay
The comment's staffing idea is a suggestion, not evaluated evidence
